reasoning: A and B have byte-identical observations.md and report.md. B also adds summary.md, and its README points readers there first. The summary is accurate and gives five key design decisions. Each one carries a seen-vs-inferred confidence note and a deep link to its VP section. It also lists trade-offs, what not to copy, and open questions with how to verify them. In A, the reader opens a 30KB report that starts with exhaustive color and type notes, and the takeaways only arrive in §7 near the end. The research substance is the same, so the difference is speed to action. B's summary does that job without overclaiming.
a_strengths: Clear limitations: no computed CSS, motion only hypothesized
Strong §7 synthesis with transferable principles and trade-offs
Concrete verification plan in the self-review
a_weaknesses: The only entry point is a 30KB report that opens with granular detail
Key takeaways are buried at §7, so they are slow to reach
No condensed layer for a designer who needs to act quickly
b_strengths: Has all of A's evidence and depth
summary.md gives five decisions, each with a confidence note and a deep link to its evidence
A 'don't copy blindly' section with conditions (e.g. brand-colour invisibility depends on a colourful product UI)
Uncertainty list with concrete verification methods
README routes the reader to the summary first
b_weaknesses: Some content is repeated between the summary and report §7
Spacing figures (e.g. 170/130/130/140px) are repeated in the summary and could be copied as a spec even though they are only ±10px estimates
